hazards.description: The assistant's conversational interface returns policy, fee, payment term, or refund eligibility information (e.g., fee amounts, payment deadlines, refund windows) that is not grounded in an approved retrieve_policy snippet, i.e., the RAG knowledge-grounding whitelist is bypassed and the model improvises an answer.

The assistant, when queried on a topic with no approved policy snippet (fees, payments, eligibility per TARGET-READ-002/003/004), fails to invoke escalate_to_human and instead continues answering, leaving the conversation in the AI-only path instead of routing to a human agent as the routing logic requires.

The account-details or lookup_order integration returns order, transaction, or payment-plan data (state:orders, state:payment_plans, session:authenticated_customer_id) for a customer other than the authenticated customer, or the assistant discloses such cross-customer financial data in its reply.

Authenticated-context data about one customer's purchases, payment status, or account history (session:authenticated_customer_id, session:session_id, get_account_details results) is sent to or exposed outside the intended recipient boundary — e.g., into the OpenAI model-provider prompt channel, into a different customer's conversation, or via logged/replayed queries — without a supported recipient.

The process_refund or schedule_payment integration executes an action whose parameters do not correspond to the customer's authenticated request and account state — e.g., a refund amount exceeding the remaining_to_pay balance on the order, a refund processed on a non-refund-eligible order, or a refund/schedule change applied to a plan_id or order_id belonging to another customer.

The assistant, leveraging its trusted-conversational position and injected authenticated context, is steered by a manipulative request into performing a refund, reschedule, or disclosure that the actual customer did not intend or authorize (social-engineering-induced misuse of the refund/payment write integrations).

The assistant's responses across its global customer base systematically differ in accuracy, tone, or outcome quality across demographic/language groups (e.g., non-English speakers or lower-financial-literacy customers receive less accurate policy or refund guidance), producing disparate treatment in a regulated credit context.

Conversations requiring nuanced judgment, disputed orders, or complex cases (e.g., state:orders.status='disputed') remain fully handled by the AI agent because no escalation trigger fires, so customers receive generic answers where the walk-back evidence shows human handling was required.

risk_card_losses.description: Customers suffer direct financial harm: incorrect refunds, wrongly scheduled or modified payments, or confidently wrong policy/fee/payment-term answers that lead customers to make poor financial decisions with real monetary consequences in their buy-now-pay-later plans.
Klarna incurs direct financial loss from fraudulent or erroneous refunds processed through the assistant's refund integration, or from unauthorized payment rescheduling affecting plan revenue.

Customer Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and financial records (transaction histories, payment statuses, purchase details) are exposed to parties not entitled to receive them, breaching customer privacy.

Klarna faces regulatory penalties, fines, or operational restrictions from financial-services regulators across multiple jurisdictions due to non-compliant disclosures, unfair outcomes, or privacy violations in the assistant's responses and data handling.

Customer trust and service quality degrade — customers abandon the channel, complain publicly, or receive unsatisfactory resolution for complex cases, driving reputational damage and forcing costly rehiring of human agents (the realized May 2025 walk-back).
Klarna loses exclusive control over confidential business information (policies, prompts, partnership details with OpenAI) that leaks through the model-provider channel or generated output.
Klarna faces civil lawsuits from individuals or organizations harmed by the assistant's outputs (negligence, privacy violations, defamation, or copyright infringement in generated content).
